title: Spec: clarify implemented template variable namespaces
description:
## Problem
`SPECIFICATION.md` documents six template variable namespaces, but only `{input.*}` and `{state.*}` are currently implemented.

| Namespace | Spec Says | Reality |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{input.*}` | Supported | Working |
| `{state.*}` | Supported | Working |
| `{output.*}` | Supported | Not implemented |
| `{context.*}` | Supported | Not implemented |
| `{prepared.*}` | Supported | Not implemented |
| `{env.*}` | Supported | Not implemented |

## Why it matters
- Users will assume `{env.*}` / `{prepared.*}` / etc. work and won’t realize substitution is not happening.

## Where this shows up
- `TECHNICAL_DEBT.md` → “Template Variable Namespaces” (Category 1).
- `SPECIFICATION.md` Template Variable Namespaces section (currently around lines 843–856).

## Proposed fix (docs-only)
- Mark unimplemented namespaces as Planned/Future (or remove until implemented).
- Explicitly state which namespaces are implemented today.

## Acceptance criteria
- `SPECIFICATION.md` clearly distinguishes implemented vs planned template namespaces.
- Examples avoid using unimplemented namespaces unless marked as future.
